questions.question: How do you publish a Spring event?
questions.explanation: Inject ApplicationEventPublisher and call publishEvent with your event object.

questions.question: By default, on which thread does a normal @EventListener run?
options: A new thread for each listener
The publisher's own thread, and the publisher waits
questions.explanation: Spring events are synchronous by default. Listeners run one after another on the thread that published.

questions.question: An OrderPlaced event has three listeners with @Order(1), @Order(2) and @Order(3), each printing its number. The publisher prints "done" after publishEvent. What is printed?
questions.explanation: Listeners run in @Order sequence on the publisher's thread, so publishEvent returns only after all three.

questions.question: A listener has condition = "#event.amountInRupees() >= 1000". An order of 350 rupees is published. What happens to that listener?
options: It runs and prints an error
It is skipped for this event
questions.explanation: When the condition is false, Spring does not call that listener. The other listeners still run.

questions.question: A normal @EventListener sends an email inside a database transaction. The transaction later rolls back, but the customer already got the email. What is the better choice?
options: Remove the listener and send the email in main
questions.explanation: @TransactionalEventListener waits for the commit by default, so side effects like email happen only if the data was saved.
